# Project workflow

Read AGENTS.md for the project workflow and Beads skill.

○ trial-0gf · Apply the approved release 2 credit agreement   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-08 · Updated: 2026-09-08

DESCRIPTION

  Meridian Credits quotes loyalty credits for a subscription reseller. The    
  local Python CLI accepts one JSON object on stdin and emits exactly one JSON
  object on stdout; run python3 main.py. Preserve {"command":"ping"} ->       
  {"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"} and the existing unknown-      
  command response. No network, clock, locale or third-party package is       
  needed. Malformed input is outside these issues.                            
                                                                              
  A charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, 
  and charge_cents. The three IDs are nonempty strings; line_id is unique     
  within a request. A subscription is identified by the pair (account_id,     
  subscription_id); the same subscription_id can occur under different        
  accounts, and a subscription can have several charge lines. service_on is a 
  valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD date from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31.         
  charge_cents is a nonnegative integer in US cents. No line is excluded by   
  its service date. Each request is the complete charge set of one            
  independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Line    
  collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID order means Unicode code-point   
  order. JSON object key order is immaterial; do not add response keys beyond 
  those specified.                                                            
                                                                              
  Release "1.0" is the initial agreement. An omitted release selects the      
  current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version.      
  Versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward. Public suites   
  name a specific release and send explicit release values, so their          
  expectations remain applicable when the current agreement changes. Run a    
  supplied suite with python3 test_public.py --cases PATH.                    
                                                                              
  Finance has permanently adopted release 2.0 as the current agreement: Each  
  line's uncapped credit is 15% of charge_cents, rounded down separately to   
  integer cents. The 3000-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same
  (account_id, subscription_id) pair. Distinct groups have independent caps.  
  Within each cap group, credit is assigned to lines in this priority: largest
  charge_cents first; equal charges use increasing line_id. Each line receives
  its uncapped credit up to the group's remaining cap; later lines receive    
  only the remaining credit, or zero. The total credit is the sum of assigned 
  line credits. A line's amount due is its charge minus its assigned credit;  
  the total due is total charges minus total credit.                          
                                                                              
  Requests to quote and total with omitted release now use release "2.0".     
  Support explicit release "2.0" with the same behavior. Explicit release     
  "1.0" quote and total requests continue to use the original approved        
  agreement. Request/response shapes are unchanged; the response release      
  identifies the agreement actually used. This replaces the current agreement 
  for every supplied charge set, regardless of service dates.                 
                                                                              
  Example current quote request: {"command": "quote", "line": {"line_id": "L- 
  1", "account_id": "A", "subscription_id": "S", "service_on": "2026-04-15",  
  "charge_cents": 19999}}                                                     
  Response: {"release": "2.0", "credit_cents": 2999, "amount_due_cents":      
  17000, "line_id": "L-1"}

Meridian Credits release 1.0 credit agreement (finance-approved in issue trial-351, 2026-09-07; statement-total command approved in issue trial-eio, 2026-09-08). Applies to all Meridian Credits quote and total requests naming release 1.0; the current agreement is 1.0, so an omitted release selects 1.0. Versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward.

Credit rules per request (a request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set):
- Uncapped credit per line: 10% of charge_cents, rounded down separately per line to integer cents (integer arithmetic charge_cents // 10).
- Cap: 2400 cents shared by ALL lines with the same account_id, across its subscriptions; distinct account_id groups have independent caps.
- Assignment priority within a cap group: earliest service_on first; equal service dates use increasing line_id (lexicographic = Unicode code-point order).
- Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group remaining cap; later lines receive only the remainder, or zero.
- Totals: total credit = sum of assigned line credits; per-line amount due = charge - assigned credit; total due = total charges - total credit.

One-line quote contract (trial-351): request {"command":"quote","line":LINE} or same with "release":"1.0"; response has exactly release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; the supplied line is treated as the entire statement. Example: charge 19999 -> credit 1999, due 18000.

Statement total contract (trial-eio): request {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...]} or same with "release":"1.0"; response has exactly release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents for the whole supplied charge set under this agreement's shared-cap scope; it is NOT a collection of independent single-line quotes. Empty lines -> {"release":"1.0","credit_cents":0,"amount_due_cents":0}; a statement of only the quote example line (charge 19999) -> credit 1999, due 18000. The quote command remains available and unchanged.

Line schema constraints: exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, charge_cents; IDs nonempty strings; line_id unique within a request; subscription identified by (account_id, subscription_id) pair; service_on valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD in 2020-01-01..2099-12-31; charge_cents nonnegative integer US cents; no line excluded by service date; line collections may be empty; JSON key order immaterial; no response keys beyond those specified.

CLI contract: python3 main.py reads one JSON object on stdin, writes exactly one JSON object on stdout. {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"}; unknown command -> {"error":"unknown_command"}. No network/clock/locale/third-party packages; malformed input out of scope.

Implementation notes beyond the agreement text (inference, not finance-approved): main.py implements the full multi-line assignment (assign_credits) so the shared-cap priority order is available to later commands; a release value outside SUPPORTED_RELEASES returns {"error":"unsupported_release"} for quote and total alike. For a single account group the total assigned credit equals min(sum of per-line uncapped credits, 2400) regardless of assignment order, because greedy assignment saturates the cap; priority order still governs per-line assignment.

Verification (2026-09-08): public suites public_tests/release_1_quote.json and public_tests/release_1_total.json pass (python3 test_public.py --cases); local tests tests/test_quote.py, tests/test_total.py (empty statement, omitted release, shared cap across lines, independent caps per account, same subscription_id under different accounts, several lines of one subscription, floor rounding, zero charges, unsupported release), and tests/test_smoke.py all pass.

Source: issues trial-351 and trial-eio quoting the finance-approved release 1.0 agreement and the approved statement-total contract.

operation_argv:
Meridian Credits release 2.0 credit agreement - the CURRENT agreement, permanently adopted by finance in issue trial-0gf (2026-09-08). Applies to quote and total requests naming release "2.0" explicitly and to every request with an omitted release from trial-0gf onward, for every supplied charge set regardless of service dates. Release 1.0 remains supported for requests naming "1.0" explicitly; versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward.

Credit rules per request (a request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set):
- Uncapped credit per line: 15% of charge_cents, rounded down separately per line to integer cents (integer arithmetic charge_cents * 15 // 100).
- Cap: 3000 cents shared by ALL lines with the same (account_id, subscription_id) pair; distinct pairs have independent caps. This differs from release 1.0, whose 2400-cent cap is per account_id across its subscriptions.
- Assignment priority within a cap group: largest charge_cents first; equal charges use increasing line_id (lexicographic = Unicode code-point order). service_on does not affect priority in 2.0.
- Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group remaining cap; later lines receive only the remaining credit, or zero.
- Totals: total credit = sum of assigned line credits; per-line amount due = charge - assigned credit; total due = total charges - total credit.

Request/response shapes unchanged from release 1.0: quote {"command":"quote"[,"release"],"line":LINE} -> exactly release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; total {"command":"total"[,"release"],"lines":[LINE,...]} -> exactly release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; the response release names the agreement actually used ("2.0" here). Empty lines -> credit 0, due 0. Quote example: charge 19999 -> credit 2999 (15% = 2999.85 floored), due 17000. A release outside SUPPORTED_RELEASES ("1.0","2.0") returns {"error":"unsupported_release"} for quote and total alike.

Line schema constraints and CLI contract are as in meridian-credits/release-1.0-credit-agreement: exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, charge_cents; IDs nonempty strings; line_id unique within a request; subscription identified by the (account_id, subscription_id) pair; service_on valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD in 2020-01-01..2099-12-31; charge_cents nonnegative integer US cents; line collections may be empty; JSON key order immaterial; no response keys beyond those specified; {"command":"ping"} and unknown-command responses preserved; no network/clock/locale/third-party packages; malformed input out of scope.

Implementation notes beyond the agreement text (inference, not finance-approved): main.py implements full multi-line assignment (assign_credits_release_2_0) so per-line priority is available to later commands; as with 1.0, aggregate group credit equals min(sum of per-line uncapped credits, 3000) regardless of assignment order, so priority order is not observable through the current total command aggregate response - only through per-line results, which only the single-line quote currently exposes.

Verification (2026-09-08, issue trial-0gf): public suites public_tests/release_1_quote.json, public_tests/release_1_total.json and public_tests/release_2_quote_total.json pass via python3 test_public.py --cases; local suites tests/test_quote.py, tests/test_total.py (release 1 and 2 coverage: omitted release selects 2.0, 15% flooring, 3000 cap shared per (account, subscription) pair, independent caps per subscription of one account and for one subscription_id across accounts, cap saturation from partial credits, empty statement, zero charges, unsupported release) and tests/test_smoke.py pass, 30 tests total; per-line priority verified directly against assign_credits_release_2_0 (equal-charge tie broken by increasing line_id; later lines receive remainder or zero).

Applies to Meridian Credits quote and total requests naming release 1.0 explicitly. Since issue trial-0gf (2026-09-08) the current agreement is release 2.0, so an omitted release selects 2.0 (see meridian-credits/release-2.0-credit-agreement); before trial-0gf an omitted release selected 1.0 (see meridian-credits/current-agreement-history). Versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward.

Credit rules per request (a request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set):
- Uncapped credit per line: 10% of charge_cents, rounded down separately per line to integer cents (integer arithmetic charge_cents // 10).
- Cap: 2400 cents shared by ALL lines with the same account_id, across its subscriptions; distinct account_id groups have independent caps.
- Assignment priority within a cap group: earliest service_on first; equal service dates use increasing line_id (lexicographic = Unicode code-point order).
- Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group remaining cap; later lines receive only the remainder, or zero.
- Totals: total credit = sum of assigned line credits; per-line amount due = charge - assigned credit; total due = total charges - total credit.

One-line quote contract (trial-351): request {"command":"quote","line":LINE} or same with "release":"1.0"; response has exactly release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; the supplied line is treated as the entire statement. Example: charge 19999 -> credit 1999, due 18000.

Statement total contract (trial-eio): request {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...]} or same with "release":"1.0"; response has exactly release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents for the whole supplied charge set under this agreement shared-cap scope; it is NOT a collection of independent single-line quotes. Empty lines -> {"release":"1.0","credit_cents":0,"amount_due_cents":0}; a statement of only the quote example line (charge 19999) -> credit 1999, due 18000. The quote command remains available and unchanged.

Line schema constraints: exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, charge_cents; IDs nonempty strings; line_id unique within a request; subscription identified by (account_id, subscription_id) pair; service_on valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD in 2020-01-01..2099-12-31; charge_cents nonnegative integer US cents; no line excluded by service date; line collections may be empty; JSON key order immaterial; no response keys beyond those specified.

CLI contract: python3 main.py reads one JSON object on stdin, writes exactly one JSON object on stdout. {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"}; unknown command -> {"error":"unknown_command"}. No network/clock/locale/third-party packages; malformed input out of scope.

Implementation notes beyond the agreement text (inference, not finance-approved): main.py implements the full multi-line assignment (assign_credits_release_1_0) so the shared-cap priority order is available to later commands; a release value outside SUPPORTED_RELEASES ("1.0","2.0") returns {"error":"unsupported_release"} for quote and total alike. For a single account group the total assigned credit equals min(sum of per-line uncapped credits, 2400) regardless of assignment order, because greedy assignment saturates the cap; priority order still governs per-line assignment.

Verification (2026-09-08): public suites public_tests/release_1_quote.json and public_tests/release_1_total.json pass (python3 test_public.py --cases); local release-1.0 cases in tests/test_quote.py and tests/test_total.py pass. Re-verified 2026-09-08 in issue trial-0gf after release 2.0 became the current agreement: explicit-1.0 public suites and local release-1 tests still pass unchanged alongside the release-2 suites.

Source: issues trial-351 and trial-eio quoting the finance-approved release 1.0 agreement and the approved statement-total contract; current-agreement revision in issue trial-0gf.

stdout:
Close one or more issues.

If no issue ID is provided, closes the last touched issue (from most recent
create, update, show, or close operation). This fallback only applies in
interactive sessions (stdin is a terminal); in scripts and agent sessions a
missing ID is an error, so a command built from an empty variable cannot
silently close an unrelated issue. Set BD_LAST_TOUCHED_FALLBACK=1 to allow
the fallback anywhere, or =0 to disable it entirely.

When closing multiple issues, provide one --reason for all IDs or repeat
--reason once per ID. Reasons map positionally: the first --reason applies
to the first ID, the second --reason to the second ID, regardless of where
the flags appear in the command line.

Usage:
  bd close [id...] [flags]

Aliases:
  close, done

Flags:
      --claim-next           Automatically claim the next highest priority available issue
      --continue             Auto-advance to next step in molecule
  -f, --force                Force close pinned issues or unsatisfied gates
  -h, --help                 help for close
      --no-auto              With --continue, show next step but don't claim it
  -r, --reason string        Reason for closing
      --reason-file string   Read close reason from file (use - for stdin)
      --session string       Claude Code session ID (or set CLAUDE_SESSION_ID env var)
      --suggest-next         Show newly unblocked issues after closing

Global Flags:
      --actor string              Actor name for audit trail (default: $BEADS_ACTOR, git user.name, $USER)
      --cpu-profile               Generate CPU profile for performance analysis
      --database string           Run against a different server database for this invocation, without changing the project's configured database (proxied-server mode only)
      --db string                 Database path (default: auto-discover .beads/*.db). In proxied-server mode, a value that isn't an existing path is treated as a database name override (see --database)
  -C, --directory string          Change to this directory before running the command (like git -C)
      --dolt-auto-commit string   Dolt auto-commit policy (off|on|batch). 'on': commit after each write. 'batch': defer commits to bd dolt commit; uncommitted changes persist in the working set until then (a live batch-mode bd process also flushes on SIGTERM/SIGHUP). Applies to embedded and direct SQL-server modes; proxied-server routes are unaffected. Default: on. Override via config key dolt.auto-commit
      --global                    Use the global shared-server database (beads_global)
      --ignore-schema-skew        Proceed despite forward schema drift (some queries may fail)
      --json                      Output in JSON format
      --mem-profile string        Write heap profile to FILE on exit (also respects BEADS_MEM_PROFILE)
      --no-color                  Disable color output (also: NO_COLOR=1 or CLICOLOR=0)
  -q, --quiet                     Suppress non-essential output (errors only)
      --readonly                  Read-only mode: block write operations (for worker sandboxes)
      --sandbox                   Sandbox mode: disables Dolt auto-push
  -v, --verbose                   Enable verbose/debug output
